title: Buildflow: validate and publish model performance manifests
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a robust CI buildflow that produces, validates, and publishes machine-readable performance manifests for newly onboarded models. These artifacts (performance-manifests) will serve as the authoritative source for latency/cost/quality profiles used by routing, autoscaling, and the Console. The flow must: build model artifacts, run standardized microbenchmarks and workload-driven profiling harnesses, synthesize a performance manifest (quantiles, p50/p95 token latency, throughput at batch sizes, memory footprint, quantization caveats), run automated validation checks against model-acceptance criteria, produce provenance metadata, cryptographically endorse the manifest, and publish to the model registry with pinning instructions for safe rollouts. This ticket focuses on the CI automation and manifest lifecycle; integration with the Console rollout UI and dedicated capacity scheduler is covered by follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: CI job produces a machine-readable performance-manifest JSON for each model artifact on successful build
Automated validators run and emit a pass/fail result with human-readable failure reasons
Provenance metadata (git SHA, build image, runner id, benchmark seed) is included in the manifest
Manifest is cryptographically endorsed and published to the registry with a unique immutable URI
A pin record linking the model artifact and manifest can be created via API and appears in the model-registry UI
A rollback key exists to mark manifest as revoked and trigger automatic model fallback in runtime
implementation_notes: Use existing CI fleet (buildkite) and create a dedicated pipeline step `profiling/manifest`
Benchmark harness should reuse perf harness used by runtime-telemetry to reduce duplication
Validate numeric stability by running profiling 3 times and reporting medians; include raw samples in artifact
Adopt Sigstore/cosign for manifest endorsement; store signatures alongside manifest in registry-store
Manifest schema v1 with explicit fields for hardware-profile, model-shape, tokenizer, quantized-variant and sanitized notes
Protect secret keys via KMS integration already used by release bridge; rotate keys via existing vault policy
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge pipeline and enable for a small set of non-production models (canary-models)
Step 2: Validate end-to-end publishing and pinning for 3 target models; confirm Console displays manifest and provenance
Step 3: Run 2-week shadow validation comparing runtime routing decisions using published manifests vs current heuristics
Step 4: Gradual expansion to all new onboarded models; block auto-publish for models with failed validation
Rollback: Revoke manifest signature and mark pin as deprecated; runtime falls back to pinned previous manifest/variant
risks: Profiling runs may add significant CI time and cost — need caching and selective re-profiling heuristics
False negatives in validators could block safe models; validators must provide clear triage info
Key management mistakes during endorsement could invalidate many manifests — require key rotation rehearsals
Schema changes to manifest could require coordinated runtime and Console updates; include feature flags

2025-11-20: Proposal reviewed with Runtime team; agreed on manifest schema v1 fields and versioning approach. Action: add `hardware_profile` and `quantization_notes`. - Daniel
2025-12-08: Proof-of-concept pipeline wired into Buildkite. Profiling step runs but median aggregation not yet implemented; manifests stored in temporary S3 path. - Daniel

2026-01-12: Security reviewed the endorsement plan; recommended Sigstore + KMS-backed cosign integration and killed plans to embed raw keys in CI images. Follow-up: create key rotation runbook. - Leah Morris

2026-02-04: Added automated validators for token-latency regression (p95 threshold), throughput floor checks, and memory spike detection. Two models failed throughput check — investigation shows quantization flag mismatch. - Daniel

2026-03-01: Manifest signature flow finalized; cosign integration merged. Registry endpoint updated to accept signed manifests and produce immutable URIs. Need to update Console to show signature status. - Maya

2026-03-10: Enabling canary for 3 models; end-to-end publish+pin flow exercised. One edge case: duplicate manifest versions created when CI retried; addressing by dedup key using git SHA + artifact digest. Next: harden dedup and add alerts on duplicate uploads. - Daniel
